subject: Nguyen et al. (2018)
object: Nguyen et al. (2018) identified biallelic deleterious mutations in MEI1, TOP6BL/C11orf80, and REC114 in women with recurrent androgenetic complete hydatidiform moles. These genes have roles in forming meiotic double-strand breaks.

subject: Nguyen et al. (2018)
object: Nguyen et al. (2018) found that 8% of oocytes from Mei1-deficient female mice lost all their chromosomes by extruding them, together with the spindles, into the first polar body. Mei1-/- oocytes could be fertilized, and 5% produced androgenetic zygotes. The authors proposed that extrusion of all maternal chromosomes is a mechanism for producing androgenetic zygotes.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) performed whole-genome sequencing in 39 men with nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA). Six of them had previously had uninformative whole-exome sequencing. All 39 had a normal karyotype and no Y chromosome microdeletions or CFTR mutations. Using a recessive model (hemizygous, homozygous or compound heterozygous) and filtering at gnomAD VAF < 0.01, the authors identified candidate NOA-associated variants in 29 of the 39 men, and in 5 of the 6 men with prior negative exome sequencing.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) classified the testicular biopsies of the NOA patients by histopathology and Johnsen score: 16 showed postmeiotic arrest (Johnsen 6-9), 3 meiotic arrest (Johnsen 4-5), 3 premeiotic arrest (Johnsen 3), and 10 Sertoli cell-only syndrome (Johnsen 2).

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) identified 2 ultrarare variants in the X-linked TKTL1 gene (Xq28) in 2 men with NOA, both predicted to be disease causing. One was c.268_268delG (p.Asp90Metfs*35), found in a patient with meiotic arrest; the other was c.1601A>G (p.Glu534Gly), located in the C-terminal domain. Neither variant was found in gnomAD. Neither patient showed TKTL1 expression at the mRNA or protein level. Structural modeling suggested that the Glu534Gly change destabilizes the fold of the C-terminal domain, which helps mediate homodimerization.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) identified 4 hemizygous variants in the X-linked IGSF1 gene (Xq26.1) in 4 of 39 men with NOA. These were c.758A>G (p.Tyr253Cys) in patient P31L, who had Sertoli cell-only syndrome; c.1184T>G (p.Leu395Arg) in P10L, who had postmeiotic arrest; c.2554T>G (p.Tyr838Asp) in P45L, who had postmeiotic arrest; and the intronic variant g.114567C>G in P41P, who had meiotic arrest. Three of the 4 variants had not been reported in ClinVar; c.1184T>G was listed there as benign. Homology modeling suggested that Leu395Arg would deform the Ig domain fold.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) identified compound heterozygous ZFPM2 variants, c.89A>G (p.Glu30Gly) and c.2287G>A (p.Val763Ile), in patient P10L, who had NOA with postmeiotic arrest. The c.2287G>A (p.Val763Ile) variant was also found in the homozygous state in a second patient with postmeiotic arrest (P9L). All of these variants were predicted in silico to be disease causing. The authors noted that c.89A>G had previously been associated with 46,XY sex reversal-3.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) identified an ultrarare hemizygous VCX3A variant, c.556G>A (p.Val186Met), in a man with NOA and Sertoli cell-only syndrome. VCX3A is located at Xp22.31 and is expressed only in the testis.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) found biallelic rare variants in autosomal genes previously linked to infertility in individual NOA patients. These were TEX14 c.2285_2288delAGAA (homozygous); and compound heterozygous variants in DNAH1 (c.8455G>A, c.11494_11495delinsAG), FANCM (g.19521G>A, c.2081T>G), FSIP2, PMFBP1, MEI1 (c.1546A>G, c.3542G>A), PIWIL1 and WDR66. A homozygous QRICH2 variant was also found.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) found ultrarare ESX1 variants (c.1040C>G, c.1042C>G) and a TEX13A variant (c.596G>A) in NOA patients with postmeiotic arrest. The authors noted that the ESX1 variants resemble variants previously reported in Han Chinese men with NOA (c.1094C>G, c.1096C>G). They predicted that the ESX1 variants would destabilize cyclins.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) also found rare hemizygous variants in X-linked genes previously implicated in infertility. These included KCND1 c.1723T>G, KIAA1210 c.1214G>A, FAM47C c.1826A>G, ZMYM3 c.2367C>G and FANCB c.1769T>C. They also found a homozygous FAM50B variant, c.293G>A, in patient P9L, who had postmeiotic arrest.

subject: Malcher et al. (2022)
object: Malcher et al. (2022) observed marked genetic heterogeneity among the NOA patients: of the 29 men with candidate variants, only 2 (in one case 3) shared the same variant. Sixteen of the 58 rare variants had not been reported before.

subject: Chen et al. (2023)
object: Chen et al. (2023) reported 2 Chinese brothers with infertility due to cryptozoospermia. The proband, a 30-year-old man with 5 years of infertility, had normal external genitalia, bilateral testicular volumes of about 12 ml, and normal semen volume and pH; no sperm were seen in the initial semen smear, but centrifuged sediment showed 0-1 sperm per high-power field (10-15 sperm in 20 HPF), few of them motile. Serum FSH, LH, testosterone, estradiol, prolactin, inhibin B, and AMH were normal, the karyotype was 46,XY, and there were no Y-chromosome AZF microdeletions. His brother had 3 years of infertility and also had cryptozoospermia, with normal physical examination, hormones, karyotype, and Y-microdeletion testing.

subject: Chen et al. (2023)
object: In 2 Chinese brothers with cryptozoospermia, Chen et al. (2023) identified compound heterozygous variants in the MEI1 gene: a c.529+5G>A splice site variant downstream of exon 5 (predicted to affect splicing) and a c.2071C>G transversion in exon 18 resulting in a gln691-to-glu (Q691E) substitution. The variants, found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing, were absent from ExAC and gnomAD. The father was heterozygous for the missense variant and the mother for the splice variant; the father had normal fertility. Testicular tissue and sperm were not available for functional study.

subject: Chen et al. (2023)
object: Chen et al. (2023) suggested that the combination of the two MEI1 variants may permit slight MEI1 expression, sometimes allowing meiosis to occur and resulting in cryptozoospermia rather than nonobstructive azoospermia.

subject: Chen et al. (2023)
object: Chen et al. (2023) stated that the MEI1 variants in the affected brothers were inherited from parents who were each heterozygous carriers, indicating autosomal recessive inheritance.

subject: Zhang et al. (2023)
object: Zhang et al. (2023) described 4 Chinese men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). Testicular pathologic analysis and immunohistochemical staining showed that spermatogenesis was arrested at the spermatocyte stage. The patients also had defective homeostasis of programmed DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and defective meiotic chromosome synapsis.

subject: Zhang et al. (2023)
object: Using whole-exome sequencing, Zhang et al. (2023) identified bi-allelic deleterious variants in the MEI1 gene in 4 Chinese patients with non-obstructive azoospermia and meiotic arrest. The authors concluded that bi-allelic MEI1 variants could cause defective DSB homeostasis and meiotic chromosome synapsis, which lead to meiotic arrest and male infertility.

subject: Zhang et al. (2023)
object: Zhang et al. (2023) found a missense variant in MEI1, c.G186C, as one of the bi-allelic variants in their patients with NOA. In vitro, this variant reduced MEI1 expression.

subject: Zhang et al. (2023)
object: Zhang et al. (2023) found a frameshift variant in MEI1, c.251delT, in their patients with NOA. In vitro, this variant led to truncated MEI1 proteins.

subject: Zhang et al. (2023)
object: Zhang et al. (2023) found a missense variant in MEI1, c.T1585A, in their patients with NOA. Based on bioinformatic analysis, the authors assumed that this variant affects the interaction between MEI1 and its partners.

subject: Liu et al. (2025)
object: Liu et al. (2025) described a consanguineous family in which a male infertile patient had azoospermia and a female infertile patient had embryonic arrest. Preimplantation genetic testing of the female patient's arrested embryos showed high levels of chromosomal anomalies.

subject: Liu et al. (2025)
object: In the male patient with azoospermia and the female patient with embryonic arrest from a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) used whole-exome sequencing, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, to identify a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene. Amplification and sequencing of cDNA confirmed that the exon was missing, and exon 19 expression was almost undetectable in the patients. Their mother was a heterozygous carrier. In transfected HEK293T cells, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with the predicted premature termination in exon 20. The authors stated that this was the first exon rearrangement reported in MEI1.
